correctness.rationale: For f(m)=D(m²), the prime-power coefficients f(p^a)=a+1/2 give the exact local Euler factor (1-z/2+z²/2)/(1-z)². Its regularization H_p=(1-z/2+z²/2)/(1-z)^1/2 has 1+5z²/8+O(z³), ensuring absolute convergence near s=1. Nonnegative coefficients are dominated by tau(m), so the standard two-term Selberg--Delange theorem at exponent 3/2 applies, giving coefficients H(1)/Gamma(3/2) and [Hprime(1)+(3gamma/2-1)H(1)]/Gamma(1/2). Exact square blocks and Abel summation add A/4 at second order, leading to K0=sqrt(2/pi)H(1) and K1=sqrt(2/pi)[Hprime(1)+(3gamma-1)H(1)/2]. Fraction-based independent divisor-count checks and direct block checks replayed from the package; numerical limits are not used as proof. Termwise differentiation gives -Hprime(1)/H(1)> (log 2)/2+(3 log 3)/16>1/2; the elementary estimate gamma<2/3 proves K1<0.
